correctness.rationale: For any real L4 orthogonal unit pair, expansion and Cauchy–Schwarz give B²≤A(1−A²). A two-point moment distribution realizes equality for every interior A. Strict concavity of sqrt(A−A³) proves a unique overlap minimizer at every lambda>0; exact rational algebra gives G(u), derivative proportional to a quartic P with unique zero on (0,1/sqrt(3)), so the supremum is global. Equality in Cauchy forces the asserted two pointwise ratios and weights. The actual packaged verifier reproduces the symbolic factorization, high-precision witness and 16,800 supplementary finite tests, which are not used as a proof for arbitrary measure spaces.

originality.rationale: The defining 2021 paper, inspected throughout its 10-page full text, gives general bounds and exponent-matched estimates but not the quadratic numerator on ambient L4. The closest published 2026 result proves an exact value for the different invariant mu_4(ell_4^2), using the same moment envelope but optimizing a different numerator. Its overlap value about 0.270323 differs from the new unique overlap about 0.200994; neither the exact value nor all L4 extremizers follows from the mu_4 assertion. The 2014/2017 paper concerns the classical exponent-one rectangular constant. Distinct scientific searches for aliases, parameters, polynomial and numerical value returned no stronger exact covering statement. Residual 1970 source and unindexed equivalences acknowledged.
residual_risks: The full 1970 Gastinel–Joly text was unavailable; a possible equivalent higher-generalized-exponent computation in that original source is not excluded by metadata alone.
Unindexed or differently notated later literature might contain the same quadratic-on-quartic optimization or a dominating formula; search failure is not proof of uniqueness.
No independent literature verification or independent scientific audit has been performed.
